description.en-US: The devotional writings of St. John Henry Newman, gathered after his death by Fr. William P. Neville of the Birmingham Oratory (1893). Part I: the meditations for each day of May on the Litany of Loreto, the memorandum on the Immaculate Conception, and the Novena and Litany of St. Philip. Part II: the Stations of the Cross, the Good Friday meditations, the litanies, and short prayers (Anima Christi, Ave Maris Stella, a Triduo to St. Joseph, a prayer for a happy death). Part III: the Meditations on Christian Doctrine, with a visit to the Blessed Sacrament.
description.pt-BR: Os escritos devocionais de São John Henry Newman, reunidos após a sua morte pelo pe. William P. Neville, do Oratório de Birmingham (1893). Parte I: as meditações para cada dia de maio sobre a Ladainha de Nossa Senhora, o memorando sobre a Imaculada Conceição e a novena e ladainha de São Filipe. Parte II: a Via-Sacra, as meditações da Sexta-feira Santa, as ladainhas e orações breves (Anima Christi, Ave Maris Stella, um tríduo a São José, uma oração por uma boa morte). Parte III: as Meditações sobre a doutrina cristã, com uma visita ao Santíssimo Sacramento.

sources.edition: Meditations and Devotions of the late Cardinal Newman, ed. Rev. W. P. Neville (London: Longmans, Green, 1893), as transcribed by the Newman Reader (National Institute for Newman Studies), pages meditations1 to meditations12.
sources.description: All three parts, 48 chapters: Newman Reader page numbers, navigation, and its editorial remarks are dropped; Newman's and the editor's notes are kept as footnotes (17); litanies and prayers keep their line breaks. Checked by sampled 6-word passages against the Internet Archive scan MeditationsAndDevotionsOf (Google Books copy of the 1893 edition; OCR-noise differences only). Raw page text in sources/en-US-originals/.
sources.tierEvidence: Public domain: Newman died in 1890 and the volume appeared in 1893 (and earlier editions of 1893-1953 and earlier are US-public-domain by date). The Newman Reader page footers claim copyright in the site's transcription (c) 2007 NINS; a plain transcription of a public-domain text adds no authorship under US law, and the text was checked against the independent Internet Archive scan.
